question: Baishakhi, the famous festival of Sikhs, is celebrated in which month every year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is April.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Baishakhi (also spelled Vaisakhi) is celebrated on 13 or 14 April every year, marking the solar new year and harvest festival in Punjab. (बैसाखी — अप्रैल माह)

 

• For Sikhs, the day holds special significance as it commemorates the founding of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, in 1699 at Anandpur Sahib.

 

• It is also observed as a harvest festival across northern India, celebrating the ripening of the rabi crop, and is known by different regional names such as Vishu (Kerala), Pohela Boishakh (Bengal), and Bihu (Assam).

 

• The festival falls around the time of Mesha Sankranti in the traditional solar calendar, marking the sun's entry into Aries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Gobind Singh created the Khalsa with the Panj Pyare (Five Beloved Ones) at Anandpur Sahib on Baishakhi day in 1699.

 

• Baishakhi is also an important day for Hindus and Buddhists in some regions, often linked with the solar new year.

 

NOTE

 

• February (Option 2): No major Sikh festival marking the new year falls in February; this is unrelated to Baishakhi.

 

• January (Option 3): January is associated with Lohri and Maghi, other Punjabi festivals, not Baishakhi.

 

• March (Option 4): March does not correspond to Baishakhi's traditional date of 13/14 April.

question: Chola inscriptions mention several categories of land, which of the following land was known as gifted to temples?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Devadana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Chola inscriptions, land donated or gifted to temples was recorded as Devadana ("gift of god"), a category of tax-free land assigned for the maintenance and worship of a deity. (देवदान — मंदिरों को दान की गई भूमि)

 

• Devadana lands formed a major part of the Chola temple economy, with revenues supporting rituals, priests, and temple establishments.

 

• Similarly, Brahmadeya referred to land gifted to Brahmins, often exempt from land revenue, forming agrahara settlements.

 

• Shalabhoga referred to land assigned for the maintenance of a school (shala), while Pallichchhandam referred to land donated to Jain institutions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chola administration is known for a sophisticated land revenue and village assembly system, documented extensively in the Uttiramerur inscriptions.

 

• Temple lands (Devadana) often enjoyed tax exemptions and were managed by temple committees such as the sabha or ur.

 

NOTE

 

• Shalabhoga (Option 2): This referred to land granted for the upkeep of an educational institution (a shala), not a temple.

 

• Pallichchhandam (Option 3): This was land gifted to Jain temples/institutions, distinct from Devadana.

 

• Brahmadeya (Option 4): This referred to land gifted to Brahmins individually or as a village grant, not to temples specifically.

question: Who was sworn in as the Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) by President Droupadi Murmu in August 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Suresh N. Patel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Suresh N. Patel was sworn in as the Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) by President Droupadi Murmu in August 2022. (केंद्रीय सतर्कता आयुक्त — सुरेश एन. पटेल)

 

• He is a 1985-batch IAS officer of the Gujarat cadre and had earlier served as Vigilance Commissioner before being elevated to CVC.

 

• The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), established in 1964 on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee, is the apex anti-corruption body in India, overseeing vigilance administration in central government departments.

 

• The CVC was accorded statutory status through the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CVC is a multi-member body consisting of a Central Vigilance Commissioner (chairperson) and not more than two Vigilance Commissioners, appointed by the President.

 

• The CVC submits an annual report to the President, which is placed before both Houses of Parliament.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajiv Gauba (Option 1): He is the Cabinet Secretary of India, not the CVC.

 

• Ranjit Rath (Option 2): He is the CMD of Oil India Limited, unrelated to the CVC post.

 

• Pramod Kumar (Option 3): Not the CVC sworn in August 2022; this name does not correspond to the office.

question: The appointments committee of cabinet (ACC) extended the tenure of current Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief for another year, till June 30, 2023. Who is the current chief?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samant Kumar Goel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) extended the tenure of Samant Kumar Goel, chief of the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), by one more year, till 30 June 2023. (रॉ प्रमुख — सामंत कुमार गोयल)

 

• Samant Kumar Goel, a 1984-batch Punjab-cadre IPS officer, was first appointed as RAW Secretary (Cabinet Secretariat) in 2019.

 

• RAW is India's primary external intelligence agency, established in 1968 after the 1962 Sino-Indian war and 1965 Indo-Pak war exposed gaps in India's external intelligence gathering.

 

• Around the same period, Arvind Kumar, the then Intelligence Bureau (IB) Director, was also given a tenure extension.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• RAW reports directly to the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) and is headed by a Secretary (Research) in the Cabinet Secretariat.

 

• Intelligence agencies like RAW and IB do not derive their powers from a specific parliamentary statute; they function under executive orders.

 

NOTE

 

• Mukul Rohatgi (Option 1): A former Attorney General of India, unrelated to RAW.

 

• Anil Chauhan (Option 2): He was appointed Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of India in September 2022, not RAW chief.

 

• Sunil Barthwal (Option 4): An IAS officer who served as Commerce Secretary, unrelated to RAW.

question: How many times did India organise the Commonwealth Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Once.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India has organised the Commonwealth Games only once, hosting the XIX Commonwealth Games in 2010 in New Delhi. (राष्ट्रमंडल खेल — भारत ने एक बार आयोजन किया, 2010 दिल्ली)

 

• The 2010 Delhi Games were held from 3 to 14 October 2010, and India finished second in the medal tally, behind Australia.

 

• The Commonwealth Games (earlier called the British Empire Games) is a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from the Commonwealth of Nations.

 

• The 2022 Commonwealth Games were held in Birmingham, England, where India finished 4th in the medal tally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Commonwealth Games were held in 1930 in Hamilton, Canada, then known as the British Empire Games.

 

• The Commonwealth Games Federation (CGF) is the governing body responsible for organising the Games.

 

NOTE

 

• Twice, Thrice (Options 2, 3): India has hosted the Commonwealth Games only once, in 2010; these overcount the actual number.

 

• Never (Option 4): Incorrect, as India successfully hosted the Games in 2010 in New Delhi.

question: Identify a dark-coloured amorphous substance that is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Humus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Humus is a dark-coloured, amorphous organic substance formed by the decomposition of plant and animal matter in soil; it is highly resistant to further microbial breakdown and decomposes at an extremely slow rate. (ह्यूमस — मृदा में अपघटन प्रतिरोधी पदार्थ)

 

• Humus improves soil fertility, water retention capacity, and aeration, and provides essential nutrients to plants as it slowly mineralises.

 

• It forms the final, stable stage of decomposition of organic matter in soil, distinct from partially decomposed litter.

 

• Chitin, by contrast, is a structural polysaccharide found in the exoskeletons of arthropods and fungal cell walls, not a soil decomposition product.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Humus is a key component of soil organic matter (SOM) and contributes to the dark colour of fertile topsoil (e.g., chernozem soils).

 

• The formation of humus is called humification, a process carried out by soil microorganisms.

 

NOTE

 

• Chitin (Option 1): A structural polysaccharide in insect exoskeletons and fungal walls, unrelated to soil decomposition resistance being described.

 

• Carotenoids (Option 3): These are pigments (yellow, orange, red) found in plants and some microorganisms, unrelated to soil organic matter.

 

• Colloids (Option 4): A general term for particle dispersions of a particular size range; not specifically the dark, decomposition-resistant substance described.

question: How many Indian states shares its border with Bangladesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Five.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Five Indian states share their border with Bangladesh: West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. (बांग्लादेश सीमा — पांच भारतीय राज्य)

 

• India shares the longest international land border with Bangladesh among all its neighbours, spanning approximately 4,096 km.

 

• West Bengal shares the longest stretch of this border among the five states.

 

• The border is guarded by the Border Security Force (BSF), with parts of it delimited by the historical Radcliffe Line.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India shares land borders with 7 countries: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Afghanistan (via PoK).

 

• The Land Boundary Agreement (2015) resolved long-standing enclave disputes between India and Bangladesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Three, Four (Options 1, 2): These undercount the actual number of bordering states, which is five.

 

• Six (Option 3): This overcounts; only five states — West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram — border Bangladesh.

question: Established in 1867 at Bombay, the _________sought to remove caste restrictions, abolish child marriage, and encourage the education of women, etc.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prarthana Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Prarthana Samaj was established in 1867 at Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang, with Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade later becoming its most influential leader. (प्रार्थना समाज — मुंबई, 1867)

 

• It sought to remove caste restrictions, abolish child marriage, encourage widow remarriage, and promote women's education, working within a broadly theistic, reformist framework influenced by the Brahmo Samaj.

 

• The organisation focused on social reform more than radical religious reform, emphasising monotheism and rational worship.

 

• Prominent members included R.G. Bhandarkar and N.G. Chandavarkar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 at Bombay, advocating a return to Vedic principles.

 

• The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotirao Phule in 1873 in Pune, focused on anti-caste and anti-Brahmin reform.

 

NOTE

 

• Veda Samaj (Option 1): Founded in 1864 in Madras by followers of Keshab Chandra Sen's Brahmo ideas; a South Indian body, not the 1867 Bombay organisation.

 

• Arya Samaj (Option 2): Founded in 1875, later than 1867, and by Swami Dayanand Saraswati, not matching the question's date.

 

• Satyashodhak Samaj (Option 4): Founded in 1873 in Pune by Jyotirao Phule, a different organisation and location.

question: A Hindu festival celebrated by the Tamil community that falls in the Tamil Solar Month is called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thaipusam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thaipusam is a Hindu festival celebrated predominantly by the Tamil community, falling in the Tamil month of Thai (January-February), when the star Pusam is at its highest point. (थाइपुसम — तमिल समुदाय का पर्व)

 

• The festival is dedicated to Lord Murugan (Kartikeya), and devotees carry ornate structures called Kavadi as an act of devotion and penance.

 

• Thaipusam is widely celebrated in Tamil Nadu, as well as among Tamil diaspora communities in Malaysia, Singapore, Mauritius, and Sri Lanka, notably at the Batu Caves in Malaysia.

 

• It commemorates the occasion when Goddess Parvati gave Murugan a Vel (spear) to vanquish the demon Soorapadman.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Karaga is a festival mainly celebrated in Karnataka, notably in Bengaluru, honouring Draupadi.

 

• Bihu is the harvest festival of Assam, and Onam is the harvest festival of Kerala, celebrated in the Malayalam month of Chingam.

 

NOTE

 

• Karaga (Option 1): A Karnataka festival honouring Draupadi, not linked to the Tamil solar month.

 

• Bihu (Option 2): An Assamese festival tied to the Assamese agricultural/lunar calendar, unrelated to the Tamil month.

 

• Onam (Option 3): A Kerala harvest festival following the Malayalam calendar, not the Tamil Solar Month.

question: Goods and services tax (GST) became operational from ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 July 2017.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) became operational across India from 1 July 2017, following the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016. (जीएसटी — 1 जुलाई 2017 से लागू)

 

• GST is a destination-based, multi-stage, value-added indirect tax that subsumed multiple central and state taxes such as excise duty, service tax, and VAT.

 

• It was launched at a special midnight session of Parliament on 30 June-1 July 2017, in the Central Hall of Parliament.

 

• GST is administered by the GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, with representation from all states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• GST has four main tax slabs: 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%, apart from exempted goods and special rates for items like gold.

 

• The GST Council was constituted under Article 279A of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 May 2016, 1 April 2016, 1 April 2017 (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these are the actual GST rollout date; GST was implemented on 1 July 2017.

question: Which of the following was known as an organisation of merchants in the inscriptions of the Pallavas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the inscriptions of the Pallavas, an organisation of merchants/traders was referred to as Nagaram, representing a mercantile town or trade guild body. (नगरम् — पल्लव अभिलेखों में व्यापारियों का संगठन)

 

• The Nagaram functioned as a local self-governing body of merchants involved in trade and commerce, parallel to agrarian assemblies like the Sabha and Ur.

 

• This institution continued and became more prominent under the Chola administration as well, indicating continuity of mercantile organisation in South India.

 

• The Pallava dynasty ruled parts of South India (Tamil Nadu and the Andhra region) from around the 3rd to 9th century CE, with Kanchipuram as their capital.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sabha was an assembly of Brahmin landholders in a Brahmadeya village, while the Ur was a general village assembly, typically of non-Brahmin villages.

 

• Guilds of merchants and craftsmen, such as the famous Ayyavole/Ainnurruvar guild, played a major role in South Indian trade in later centuries.

 

NOTE

 

• Sangathana (Option 2): Not a term used in Pallava inscriptions for merchant organisations; it is a generic modern word for 'organisation'.

 

• Ur (Option 3): This refers to a general village assembly, not specifically a merchants' body.

 

• Sabha (Option 4): This refers to an assembly of Brahmin landholders in an agrahara/Brahmadeya village, not a merchants' organisation.

question: Sundaram Balachander has been the main player of which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Veena.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sundaram Balachander (1927-1990) was a renowned Indian Veena player, also known for his contributions as a film director and actor. (सुन्दरम बालचंदर — वीणा वादक)

 

• He was a recipient of the Padma Bhushan and was celebrated for popularising Carnatic veena music both in India and internationally, including performances in the USA.

 

• The Veena is an ancient South Indian plucked string instrument, closely associated with Carnatic classical music and considered sacred to the goddess Saraswati.

 

• He also directed and acted in several Tamil films, showcasing versatility beyond music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other noted veena exponents include Chitti Babu and Doraiswamy Iyengar.

 

• Common veena types include the Saraswati Veena (Carnatic) and the Rudra Veena/Vichitra Veena (Hindustani).

 

NOTE

 

• Mridangam (Option 1): A percussion instrument; noted mridangam players include Palghat Mani Iyer, not Sundaram Balachander.

 

• Bansuri (Option 2): A bamboo flute; noted players include Hariprasad Chaurasia.

 

• Santoor (Option 4): A Kashmiri string instrument; noted players include Shivkumar Sharma.

question: As of 10 April 2022, who among the following is the Chief Minister of Puducherry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is N Rangasamy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of 10 April 2022, N. Rangasamy was the Chief Minister of Puducherry, leading the All India NR Congress (AINRC)-led NDA coalition government. (पुडुचेरी मुख्यमंत्री — एन. रंगासामी)

 

• He took oath as Chief Minister on 7 May 2021, following the 2021 Puducherry Legislative Assembly elections.

 

• This was his fourth term as Chief Minister of the Union Territory of Puducherry, having earlier served in 2001, 2008, and 2011.

 

• Puducherry is a Union Territory with a legislature, and its administration involves both a Lieutenant Governor and an elected Chief Minister.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Puducherry comprises four disjointed regions: Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam, located in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Andhra Pradesh respectively.

 

• The Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry around this period was Tamilisai Soundararajan.

 

NOTE

 

• RV Janakiraman (Option 2): A former Deputy Chief Minister/legislator of Puducherry, not the Chief Minister at this time.

 

• V Vaithilingam (Option 3): A Congress leader and former Chief Minister of Puducherry (2011-2016), not the incumbent as of April 2022.

 

• P Shanmugam (Option 4): An AINRC leader/minister, not the Chief Minister at this time.

question: What is the average height of troposphere?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13 km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, with an average height of about 13 km, though it varies from about 8 km at the poles to about 18 km at the equator. (क्षोभमंडल — औसत ऊंचाई लगभग 13 किमी)

 

• It is the layer where weather phenomena (clouds, rain, storms) occur, and temperature generally decreases with height within it, at a lapse rate of about 6.5°C per km.

 

• The boundary between the troposphere and the stratosphere is called the tropopause.

 

• Nearly 75% of the atmosphere's mass and almost all of its water vapour are contained within the troposphere.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The atmospheric layers in order from the surface are: Troposphere → Stratosphere → Mesosphere → Thermosphere → Exosphere.

 

• The ozone layer, which absorbs harmful UV radiation, lies within the stratosphere.

 

NOTE

 

• 20 km, 24 km, 8 km (Options 1, 3, 4): These do not match the commonly cited average tropospheric height of about 13 km; 8 km is closer to the polar minimum, not the average.

question: pH of milk of magnesia is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Milk of magnesia is an aqueous suspension of magnesium hydroxide [Mg(OH)₂], used as an antacid and laxative, with a pH of approximately 10, making it mildly alkaline/basic. (मिल्क ऑफ मैग्नीशिया — pH लगभग 10)

 

• Being basic, it neutralises excess stomach acid (hydrochloric acid), providing relief from acidity and indigestion.

 

• The pH scale ranges from 0 (highly acidic) to 14 (highly alkaline), with 7 being neutral.

 

• Other common basic/alkaline substances include soap (pH ~9-10) and sodium hydroxide (pH ~13-14).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Human blood has a pH of about 7.35-7.45, slightly alkaline.

 

• Gastric (stomach) acid has a pH of about 1.5-3.5, which milk of magnesia helps neutralise.

 

NOTE

 

• 12, 8, 14 (Options 1, 2, 4): These do not correctly represent the pH of milk of magnesia, which is approximately 10; pH 8 would be too mild, and pH 12/14 too strongly alkaline.

question: The real executive power is vested in the Council of Ministers with the _____________ as its head.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prime Minister.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Indian Constitution, the real executive power is vested in the Council of Ministers, with the Prime Minister as its head, while the President is the nominal/constitutional head of state. (वास्तविक कार्यपालिका शक्ति — प्रधानमंत्री)

 

• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President and is usually the leader of the majority party/coalition in the Lok Sabha.

 

• As per Article 74 of the Constitution, there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President, whose advice is binding on the President.

 

• This reflects India's parliamentary system of government, modelled on the British system, where the head of state (President) is different from the head of government (Prime Minister).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 75 deals with the appointment of other ministers, their term, and the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha.

 

• The President remains the formal head of the Union executive as per Article 53, but exercises powers based on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

 

NOTE

 

• Speaker of Rajya Sabha (Option 2): This is not a valid post; the Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and the Speaker heads the Lok Sabha — neither heads the Council of Ministers.

 

• Vice President (Option 3): The Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and has no executive role in the Council of Ministers.

 

• President (Option 4): The President is only the nominal/titular head; real executive power rests with the Council of Ministers led by the Prime Minister.

question: Which singer was given the Padma Shri in 2022 under the Arts category?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonu Nigam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sonu Nigam, the renowned playback singer, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 under the Arts (Music/Playback Singing) category. (पद्म श्री 2022 — सोनू निगम)

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, awarded by the President of India on the recommendation of the Padma Awards Committee, typically announced around Republic Day.

 

• Sonu Nigam has sung in multiple Indian languages and is known for hits across Bollywood films spanning several decades.

 

• The Padma Awards are given in three categories in descending order: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day (26 January) and are given in fields including art, social work, public affairs, science, medicine, and literature.

 

• Other notable Padma awardees in 2022 included Victor Banerjee (Padma Bhushan), among various fields.

 

NOTE

 

• Kumar Sanu (Option 1): Received the Padma Shri in 2009, not 2022.

 

• Udit Narayan (Option 2): Received the Padma Shri in 2009 and Padma Bhushan in 2016, not the 2022 award referenced here.

 

• Abhijeet Bhattacharya (Option 3): Has not received a Padma Shri; not the correct answer for this question.

question: What is the numerical value of a physical quantity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magnitude.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The numerical value of a physical quantity, expressed along with its unit, is called its magnitude. (परिमाण/मैग्नीट्यूड — भौतिक राशि का संख्यात्मक मान)

 

• Every physical quantity is expressed as: Physical Quantity = Magnitude × Unit (e.g., 5 kg, where 5 is the magnitude and kg is the unit).

 

• Physical quantities are broadly classified into scalar quantities (which have only magnitude, e.g., mass, speed, distance) and vector quantities (which have both magnitude and direction, e.g., velocity, force, displacement).

 

• A quantity without a specified unit would be ambiguous; hence magnitude is always tied to a unit for meaningful physical interpretation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vector quantities additionally require a direction to be fully specified, unlike scalar quantities.

 

• Examples of scalar quantities: mass, time, temperature, energy, distance, speed. Examples of vector quantities: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum.

 

NOTE

 

• Reference (Option 1): A reference (or reference frame/point) is used for defining position or direction, not the numerical value of a quantity.

 

• Direction (Option 2): Direction is relevant only for vector quantities and is a separate attribute from the numerical value.

 

• Distance (Option 3): Distance is itself an example of a physical quantity, not a general term for the numerical value of any physical quantity.

question: In March 2022, Tripura government announced _______ reservation for women in government jobs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 33 percent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In March 2022, the Tripura government announced 33 percent reservation for women in government jobs. (त्रिपुरा — महिलाओं के लिए 33 प्रतिशत आरक्षण)

 

• The announcement was made by Union Home Minister Amit Shah on behalf of the state government, as part of efforts to enhance women's participation and representation in the state's public sector employment.

 

• The decision was part of broader welfare and empowerment measures undertaken by the Government of Tripura, then headed by Chief Minister Manik Saha.

 

• Several other Indian states have also implemented women's reservation in government jobs at varying percentages, reflecting a broader national trend toward gender-inclusive public employment policy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tripura became a full-fledged state on 21 January 1972, and its capital is Agartala.

 

• Women's reservation policies also feature prominently in local self-government (Panchayati Raj institutions), where Article 243D mandates at least one-third reservation for women.

 

NOTE

 

• 20 percent, 27 percent, 10 percent (Options 1, 2, 3): These do not match the announced figure of 33 percent reservation for women in Tripura government jobs in March 2022.

question: In 1840, the Paramhans Mandali was established to work for the abolition of ‘Caste’ at ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Paramhans Mandali was established in 1840 at Bombay to work towards the abolition of caste restrictions and promote rationalist, reformist thought. (परमहंस मंडली — बॉम्बे, 1840)

 

• Members of the Paramhans Mandali secretly rejected caste distinctions and idol worship, and some even dined together across caste lines to break social taboos, though the organisation largely operated in secrecy due to social backlash.

 

• It is considered one of the earliest socio-religious reform organisations in Western India, predating better-known bodies like the Prarthana Samaj (1867).

 

• Members of the Paramhans Mandali later influenced or overlapped with figures associated with subsequent reform movements in Bombay.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bombay (present-day Mumbai) was a major centre of 19th-century socio-religious reform movements, also home to the Prarthana Samaj (1867) and Arya Samaj (1875).

 

• Other early reform-oriented associations of the period include the Paramahamsa Sabha, sometimes referenced interchangeably with the Paramhans Mandali in different historical accounts.

 

NOTE

 

• Lahore (Option 1): Associated with later reform activities in Punjab (e.g., some Arya Samaj branches), not the 1840 Paramhans Mandali.

 

• Calcutta (Option 2): The centre of Bengal Renaissance reform movements like the Brahmo Samaj (1828), not the Paramhans Mandali.

 

• Surat (Option 3): Not linked to the founding of the Paramhans Mandali, which was established in Bombay.

question: In football, when the ball strikes the frame of the goal or the referee and remains within the goal and touch lines, it is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is still in play.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Laws of the Game (FIFA/IFAB), in football, if the ball rebounds from the goalpost, crossbar, or corner flagpost, or off the referee/an assistant referee, and remains within the field of play (goal and touch lines), the game continues — this is termed "still in play". (फुटबॉल — गेंद पोस्ट/रेफरी से टकराकर मैदान में रहे तो 'खेल जारी')

 

• This rule ensures that incidental contact with fixed goal structures or match officials does not unfairly stop or restart play unless the ball actually crosses the boundary lines.

 

• The goal line and touchlines define the boundary of the field of play; the ball is considered out of play only when it wholly crosses these lines, whether on the ground or in the air.

 

• This law is part of the standardised 17 Laws of the Game maintained by the International Football Association Board (IFAB).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A goal is scored only when the whole of the ball passes over the goal line, between the goalposts and under the crossbar, provided no infringement has occurred.

 

• The game is officiated by a referee, assisted by assistant referees (linesmen) and, in top-tier matches, a VAR (Video Assistant Referee) system.

 

NOTE

 

• Foul (Option 1): A foul refers to an infringement of the rules (e.g., illegal contact), not the ball rebounding off the goal frame or referee.

 

• A misconduct (Option 3): Misconduct refers to player behaviour warranting a caution or sending-off, unrelated to this scenario.

 

• Out of play (Option 4): The ball is out of play only when it fully crosses the goal or touch lines, not when it rebounds and stays within the field.

question: The Indian Institute of remote sensing was established at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dehradun.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS) was established at Dehradun, Uttarakhand, and functions as a unit of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). (भारतीय सुदूर संवेदन संस्थान — देहरादून)

 

• IIRS provides education and training in remote sensing, geoinformatics, and GIS (Geographic Information System) technology and their applications in natural resource management.

 

• It was established in 1966 (originally as the Indian Photo-Interpretation Institute) and was later reorganised as IIRS in 1983 under the Department of Space.

 

• IIRS plays a key role in capacity building for India's space-based earth observation programmes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• ISRO's headquarters is located in Bengaluru, while its various centres are spread across India, e.g., Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (Thiruvananthapuram) and Satish Dhawan Space Centre (Sriharikota).

 

• Survey of India, India's oldest scientific department, is also headquartered in Dehradun.

 

NOTE

 

• Khadakwasla (Option 1): Home to the National Defence Academy (NDA), not IIRS.

 

• Shimla (Option 2): Not associated with the establishment of IIRS.

 

• Kochi (Option 4): Not associated with the establishment of IIRS.

question: 'Modernisation’ as a goal of planning in context of the Indian economy was NOT aimed at:
option_3: increase in production of goods and services
solution_text:
The correct answer is adopting a Western lifestyle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As a goal of economic planning in India, 'Modernisation' was NOT aimed at adopting a Western lifestyle; rather, it referred to the adoption of new technology, structural change in the economy, and changes in social outlook. (आधुनिकीकरण — पश्चिमी जीवनशैली अपनाना लक्ष्य नहीं था)

 

• Modernisation, as a planning goal in the Indian Five-Year Plans, meant a shift from traditional methods of production to modern techniques, along with changes in institutional and social organisation (e.g., banking systems, gender equality).

 

• It included aspects such as increase in the share of industry in national income, diversification of economic activities, advancement in technology, and change in social outlook, such as recognising the role of women in nation-building.

 

• Modernisation is often confused with Westernisation, but the two are conceptually distinct — modernisation is about progress and the rational adoption of new methods, not imitation of a particular cultural lifestyle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four major goals of Indian Five-Year Plans are commonly identified as: Growth, Modernisation, Self-Reliance, and Equity.

 

• This distinction (modernisation vs westernisation) is a standard concept covered in NCERT Class XI/XII Economics textbooks on Indian economic development.

 

NOTE

 

• Change in social outlook (Option 2): This IS a recognised part of the modernisation goal (e.g., women's participation), hence not the correct answer to 'NOT aimed at'.

 

• Increase in production of goods and services (Option 3): This IS one of the aims of modernisation, so it does not fit as the 'NOT aimed at' answer.

 

• Use of new technology (Option 4): This IS a central component of modernisation, hence not the correct answer to 'NOT aimed at'.

question: In 1664, who discovered the fifth star in the Trapezium, an asterism (mini-constellation) in the constellation Orion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Robert Hooke.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1664, Robert Hooke discovered the fifth star in the Trapezium, a compact asterism (mini-constellation) of young stars located in the Orion Nebula, within the constellation Orion. (ट्रेपेज़ियम का पांचवां तारा — रॉबर्ट हुक, 1664)

 

• The Trapezium Cluster (Theta¹ Orionis) is a tight group of hot, young stars that illuminate the surrounding Orion Nebula (M42), one of the most studied star-forming regions in the sky.

 

• Robert Hooke (1635-1703) was an English polymath scientist known for his contributions to physics (Hooke's Law), microscopy (coining the term 'cell'), and astronomy.

 

• The original four stars of the Trapezium had been known earlier, and the discovery of the fifth star added to the understanding of this multiple-star system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Orion Nebula (M42) is visible to the naked eye and is one of the brightest nebulae in the night sky, located in the 'sword' of the Orion constellation.

 

• Robert Hooke is also known for his work Micrographia (1665), a landmark publication in microscopy.

 

NOTE

 

• George Willis Ritchey (Option 1): An American astronomer known for advances in astrophotography and telescope design (Ritchey-Chrétien telescope), not the 1664 Trapezium discovery.

 

• Giordano Bruno (Option 2): An Italian philosopher/astronomer from the 16th century known for cosmological theories, not connected to this discovery.

 

• Johannes Kepler (Option 3): Known for his laws of planetary motion, not the discovery of the Trapezium's fifth star.

question:
Match column A with column B.

Column A

i. Kwashiorkor

ii. Weak bones and muscles

iii. Anaemia

iv. Goitre

Column B

a. Iodine deficiency

b. Iron deficiency

c. Calcium deficiency

d. Protein deficiency
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct matching is: i. Kwashiorkor - d. Protein deficiency; ii. Weak bones and muscles - c. Calcium deficiency; iii. Anaemia - b. Iron deficiency; iv. Goitre - a. Iodine deficiency. (कुपोषण रोग — प्रोटीन, कैल्शियम, आयरन, आयोडीन की कमी)

 

• Kwashiorkor is a severe form of protein-energy malnutrition, common in children, caused by protein deficiency, characterised by oedema, a swollen belly, and stunted growth.

 

• Weak bones and muscles result from calcium deficiency, since calcium is essential for bone mineralisation and mineral density (its prolonged deficiency causes osteoporosis/osteomalacia in adults and rickets in children).

 

• Anaemia, characterised by a reduced number of red blood cells or low haemoglobin, is primarily caused by iron deficiency, since iron is a key component of haemoglobin.

 

• Goitre, the enlargement of the thyroid gland, is caused by iodine deficiency, since iodine is essential for the synthesis of thyroid hormones (thyroxine).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other protein deficiency disorders include Marasmus, caused by a deficiency of both protein and calories, typically seen in infants.

 

• Iodised salt is commonly used as a public health measure to prevent goitre and other iodine-deficiency disorders.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-c, ii-b, iii-d, iv-a): Incorrectly pairs kwashiorkor with calcium deficiency and swaps iron and protein between weak bones/muscles and anaemia.

 

• Option 2 (i-b, ii-a, iii-c, iv-d): Incorrectly pairs kwashiorkor with iron deficiency and goitre with protein deficiency, among other mismatches.

 

• Option 4 (i-b, ii-c, iii-a, iv-d): Incorrectly pairs kwashiorkor with iron deficiency and anaemia with iodine deficiency, though it does correctly pair weak bones/muscles with calcium deficiency.
